subject: Information Theory
title: Unicity Distance
description: A quick, practical guide to Unicity Distance.

hook.text: How much ciphertext does an attacker need before only one possible key remains? That's the unicity distance.

buildup.text: Shannon calculated it: key entropy divided by plaintext redundancy. English has about 1.5 bits of entropy per letter.

discovery.text: For a simple substitution cipher, about 25 ciphertext letters suffice. After that, only one key fits.

twist.text: The one-time pad has infinite unicity distance. No amount of ciphertext narrows the key possibilities.

climax.text: Unicity distance quantifies how much data an attacker needs. It bridges information theory and cryptanalysis.

punchline.text: Enough ciphertext and only one key survives.

quiz.question: What does unicity distance measure?
options: How much ciphertext is needed to uniquely determine the key
